Cc:

Subject: Confidential: draft focused growth plan for Ethan Park — review requested

Hi Neha and Laura,

I’m preparing to move forward with a focused growth plan for Ethan Park (Eng, IC, reports to me). Before I share anything with Ethan, can you please review the attached draft plan and the evidence packet I pulled together? Key asks:

- Laura: legal sign-off on wording that sets expectations and includes the usual appeal/acknowledgement language. Any specific phrasing you recommend for the acknowledgment step?
- Neha: confirm HR compliance steps we must follow (notice timing, who needs copies, required evidence retention). Also: do we need People Ops present at the initial meeting or is manager-led appropriate with a follow-up by HR?

Attached: focused-growth-plan-ethan-park-draft-v1.docx (plan), evidence-summary-2026-05.zip (examples of missed milestones, dated PR and ticket links).

High-level timeline I’m proposing (flexible pending your guidance):
- Week 0: HR/legal review
- Week 1: Manager meeting to present plan to Ethan
- 1-month checkpoints (weekly 1:1s documented)
- 90-day review

I want to be careful and consistent here — the issues are performance-related (missed deliverables, repeated missed deadlines on the payment-sync project) but not disciplinary beyond constructive support. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confidential: draft focused growth plan for Ethan Park — review requested

Soojin —

Thanks for the draft and the evidence packet. I reviewed the document and have a few suggested edits:

1) Acknowledgment language: add a short paragraph that explains this is a performance-support plan (not a disciplinary notice) but that failure to meet objectives may lead to further action. Use neutral language: "This Performance Support Plan documents agreed objectives, measurable success criteria, and check-in cadence. Continued inability to meet objectives may result in additional steps under Redwood's corrective action policy."

2) Confidentiality/recipients: confirm we keep the plan in People Ops case file only; avoid attaching the full evidence zip to the initial meeting invite. Reference the evidence in the plan and offer to share details in the meeting.

3) Dates & notice: ensure dates are clear and that the employee gets at least 48 hours notice with the plan in writing ahead of the meeting.

4) Signatures: include a signature line for People Ops to confirm that the process has been reviewed.

I’ve made inline comments in the doc (see Drive link). If you want, I can redline the doc directly and send back. No legal blockers from my side if we adopt the neutral phrasing above and keep the evidence internal until the meeting.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confidential: draft focused growth plan for Ethan Park — review requested

Thanks — I reviewed both attachments and Laura's notes. A few HR items to confirm:

- People Ops presence: I recommend HR attend the initial meeting to observe and ensure we follow the notice & documentation requirements. I can join either in person or via Zoom.
- Notice period: provide the written plan at least 48 hours before the meeting (as Laura noted).
- Evidence handling: keep the evidence packet in the People Ops case file; do not include it in the calendar invite. We can provide summary bullet points in the plan and say detailed artifacts will be provided in the meeting.
- Accommodations: ask Ethan if there are any temporary accommodations or context we should be aware of (e.g., leave, personal risks).

I also attached a short HR checklist for managers (link in Drive). From my side, I can own scheduling and the HR confirmation signature once the final doc is ready.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of People Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks again,
Soojin
